lines: Figs from Magdala! Dried fish from the lake! Ah, a neighbor with open ears.
Tell me, do you want to hear the strangest thing I have seen in thirty years of walking these roads?
Your loss. It will keep until you are curious.
I came up the Jordan road. All the way, the road was thick with people: Jerusalem folk, Judaeans, even a few soldiers, all walking out into the wilderness.
A man is out there preaching beside the river. John, they call him. They say he wears camel's hair and lives on locusts and wild honey, though I did not get near enough to see his supper.
He cries out, 'Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand!' And those who confess their sins, he plunges beneath the river. Baptizes them, he calls it.
I believe my own eyes. The road was as busy as a feast day. As for the man's message, I only sell figs. But I have never seen so large a crowd go so quiet.
Ask Elder Ezra, he knows the Scriptures better than anyone in Kefar Zayit. And there is a woman resting by the east road, Hannah. She walked up from that country. Ask her what she saw.
Still turning it over? Well, the road east is open when you are ready. But buy something first. Figs? No? Hm.
